name: AcpiDbEvaluateOnePredefinedName
prose: Slice cut the head: static ACPI_STATUS AcpiDbEvaluateOnePredefinedName(ACPI_HANDLE ObjHandle, UINT32 NestingLevel, void *Context, void **ReturnValue) is at dbtest.c:1199-1340 (the packet name AcpiDbExecuteCallback is not in the file); it is a namespace-walk callback with Context an ACPI_DB_EXECUTE_WALK. Precondition: ObjHandle is a namespace node and Context points to the walk info with valid Count and MaxCount. Postcondition: it returns AE_OK without evaluating anything if the node's name is not a predefined name (1224-1228), if the node type is ACPI_TYPE_LOCAL_SCOPE (1230-1233), or if AcpiNsGetNormalizedPathname returns NULL (1235-1239); it frees Pathname and returns the failure status when AcpiGetObjectInfo fails (1243-1248). Otherwise, if the object is a method, it builds ACPI-required default arguments for the predefined method's argument list (integer 1, a fixed string, a garbage buffer of length 48, an empty package, or an 'Unsupported argument type' message and a skipped slot for any other type, 1253-1310), frees ObjInfo (1312), sets AcpiGbl_MethodExecuting = TRUE, calls AcpiEvaluateObject with an ACPI_ALLOCATE_BUFFER return buffer (whose contents are not freed here), prints '<Pathname> returned <status>', clears AcpiGbl_MethodExecuting, frees Pathname, discards the evaluation status (Status = AE_OK, 1329), increments Info->Count and returns AE_CTRL_TERMINATE if Info->Count >= Info->MaxCount, else AE_OK (1333-1339). A non-method predefined node is evaluated with zero parameters by the same path.
note: dbtest.c:1199-1340, slice cut head; read the head (1199-1286) and the tail (1286-1340). Old prose assumed the node was a method; in fact non-method predefined objects are also evaluated, and the early AE_OK returns (1227, 1232, 1238) and the AcpiGetObjectInfo failure return (1247) were missing. Reviewer reason was the name only.

name: AcpiDmCheckForSymbolicOpcode
prose: Slice cut the head and the packet name is not in the file: the function is BOOLEAN AcpiDmCheckForSymbolicOpcode(ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op, ACPI_OP_WALK_INFO *Info) at dmcstyle.c:207-691. Precondition: Op is a parse node whose AML opcode may be a disassembler-supported operator; the function reads Op's first argument and the next siblings; for AML_DIVIDE_OP it dereferences a fourth operand (Target2 = Target->Common.Next, 430-432) without a NULL check, so a Divide with fewer than four operands is not handled. Postcondition: it returns FALSE at once if AcpiGbl_CstyleDisassembly is false (220-223) or Op has no first argument (227-231). It then switches on the AML opcode to choose an operator symbol: arithmetic, shift, bitwise and logical operators get ' + ', ' - ' and so on; LOGICAL_NOT examines its argument (EQUAL, GREATER, LESS become ' != ', ' <= ', ' >= ' and the argument's first child gets that symbol and TRUE is returned, 303-343; any other argument prints '!' and returns TRUE, 323-328, or returns FALSE if the grandchild is missing, 336-340); INDEX returns FALSE with ACPI_PARSEOP_CLOSING_PAREN when the first argument is a string, buffer or package (352-358), else sets ' [' and ']' on the two arguments; DECREMENT and INCREMENT use '--' and '++'; BIT_NOT and STORE use no symbol; any other opcode returns FALSE (382-384). If Argument1 is marked as an LNOT suffix it returns TRUE (386-389); otherwise it sets Argument1's operator symbol if none is set. A second switch then handles targets: for the binary arithmetic/bitwise/shift opcodes it finds the target operand (for DIVIDE the first target is the remainder and the fourth the quotient, with different handling by AcpiGbl_DoDisassemblerOptimizations), returns FALSE after marking ACPI_PARSEOP_LEGACY_ASL_ONLY when the target(s) are real targets without optimisation, returns FALSE if no target remains (485-488), breaks out to the final '(' for a placeholder target, otherwise promotes the target with AcpiDmPromoteTarget and, for commutative operators (and for the non-commutative ones when the target equals the first operand), converts the operation into a compound assignment (TRUE returned, 506-563), else sets the target symbol ' = (' (possibly printing '(' for a parent operator) and returns TRUE (574-603); DECREMENT/INCREMENT return TRUE; INDEX promotes a valid target and returns TRUE (611-625); STORE returns FALSE if the optimisation is ignored or there is no target, else promotes the target with symbol ' = ' and returns TRUE (627-656); BIT_NOT with a valid target gets ' = ~' else prints '~' and returns TRUE (658-681). The final fall-through prints '(' and returns TRUE (689-690). It prints through AcpiOsPrintf and modifies flags and symbols on the parse tree; it allocates nothing.
note: dmcstyle.c:207-691. PARTLY READ: all of the function was read through a filter that dropped comment lines; the DIVIDE target selection (429-480) and the compound-assignment conditions (524-563) are summarised from that read. Round-17 reviewer RIGHT: for AML_DIVIDE_OP Target2 = Target->Common.Next is dereferenced (430-432, 458-459) without a NULL check. Slice cut head; name outside slice.

name: AcpiDsGetFieldNames
prose: Slice cut the head: static ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsGetFieldNames(ACPI_CREATE_FIELD_INFO *Info, ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState, ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Arg) is at dsfield.c:432-623. Precondition: Info describes the field being created (FieldBitPosition, FieldNode, ResourceBuffer and so on), Arg is the head of the field element list (it may be NULL, which returns AE_OK). Postcondition: it walks Arg and its Next peers while Arg is non-NULL and switches on each element's AML opcode. AML_INT_RESERVEDFIELD_OP computes Position = FieldBitPosition + element size in 64 bits and returns AE_SUPPORT if that exceeds ACPI_UINT32_MAX (473-477), else advances Info->FieldBitPosition. AML_INT_ACCESSFIELD_OP and AML_INT_EXTACCESSFIELD_OP set the access type and attributes in Info (483-511). AML_INT_CONNECTION_OP clears Info->ResourceBuffer, Info->ConnectionNode and Info->PinNumberIndex (518-520), then for a byte-list connection sets ResourceBuffer and ResourceLength from the list (527-531), while for a named connection it looks the name up with AcpiNsLookup into Info->ConnectionNode and returns the lookup failure status; ResourceLength is not cleared or set in the named case (532-546). AML_INT_NAMEDFIELD_OP looks the field name up with AcpiNsLookup in the field's node, returning the failure status (557-561); on success it sets Arg->Common.Node and Info->FieldBitLength and, only if the node has no attached object yet, calls AcpiExPrepFieldValue (returning its failure status); in iASL builds it also does an init-file lookup (583-590); it then computes Position as above and returns AE_SUPPORT if it exceeds ACPI_UINT32_MAX (597-605, after the namespace node and field object were already created, with no rollback), else adds the field bit length to FieldBitPosition and increments PinNumberIndex (608-609). Any other opcode logs 'Invalid opcode in field list' and returns AE_AML_BAD_OPCODE (612-617). When the list is exhausted it returns AE_OK (623).
note: dsfield.c:432-623 read in full except message lines. Orig reviewer RIGHT (AE_SUPPORT after the named field was looked up and its field object prepared, 574-605, no rollback); round-15 reviewer RIGHT (named Connection leaves Info->ResourceLength untouched, 532-546, so the earlier ResourceLength may persist). Slice cut head.

name: AcpiDsInitOneObject
prose: Precondition: ObjHandle is a namespace node, Context points to an ACPI_INIT_WALK_INFO (dsinit.c:193-294; it is a namespace-walk callback whose Level and ReturnValue arguments are unused). Postcondition: it returns AE_OK on every path (215, 293); nothing in this function returns an error. If the node's OwnerId differs from Info->OwnerId it returns at once without any change (213-216). Otherwise it increments Info->ObjectCount and switches on AcpiNsGetType: for ACPI_TYPE_REGION it calls AcpiDsInitializeRegion(ObjHandle), only logs an exception if that fails (the status is not returned), and increments Info->OpRegionCount (224-235); for ACPI_TYPE_METHOD it increments MethodCount, takes the attached operand object and stops there if there is none; if the method is already ACPI_METHOD_SERIALIZED it increments SerialMethodCount; otherwise, when AcpiGbl_AutoSerializeMethods is set it calls AcpiDsAutoSerializeMethod and, if the method then has the serialized flag, increments SerialMethodCount and SerializedMethodCount; any method not counted as serial increments NonSerialMethodCount (237-277); for ACPI_TYPE_DEVICE it increments DeviceCount (279-282); other types do nothing. So methods can be auto-serialized by this function but it does not itself initialise them.
note: dsinit.c:193-294 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT that AE_OK is always returned (all returns are AE_OK). Round-15 reviewer WRONG: there is a case ACPI_TYPE_DEVICE that increments DeviceCount (279-282).

name: AcpiDsIsResultUsed
prose: Slice cut the head: BOOLEAN (UINT8) AcpiDsIsResultUsed(ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op, ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState) is at dsutils.c:295-441 (name present in the file). Precondition: WalkState is valid (WalkState->ResultObj and ControlState are read). Postcondition: if Op is NULL it logs an ACPI_ERROR 'Null Op' and returns TRUE immediately, before anything else (306-310). Otherwise it first calls AcpiDsDoImplicitReturn(WalkState->ResultObj, WalkState, TRUE) and ignores its status (321). It then returns FALSE if the Op has no parent or its parent is AML_SCOPE_OP (method-level result, 331-340) and FALSE after an ACPI_ERROR if the parent's opcode class is AML_CLASS_UNKNOWN (345-350). Otherwise it decides from the parent's class: CONTROL parents give TRUE for AML_RETURN_OP and, for IF and WHILE, TRUE only when the control state is ACPI_CONTROL_PREDICATE_EXECUTING and its PredicateOp is Op, otherwise FALSE (360-393); CREATE parents give TRUE (395-400); NAMED_OBJECT parents give TRUE only when the parent opcode is a Region, DataRegion, Package, Buffer, VarPackage, EvalSubtree or BankField op, otherwise FALSE (402-419); all other classes give TRUE (421-426). The function changes no state other than whatever AcpiDsDoImplicitReturn does and the debug prints.
note: dsutils.c:295-441 read in full except debug lines. Orig reviewer RIGHT (NULL Op returns TRUE, 309); round-15 reviewer RIGHT: that return happens before AcpiDsDoImplicitReturn (321), so the implicit-return offer does not happen for a NULL Op.

name: AcpiDsExecEndOp
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsExecEndOp(ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState) at dswexec.c:500-928 (slice cut the head). Precondition: WalkState->Op and WalkState->OpInfo are non-NULL (read at 517-519 without a check). Postcondition: returns AE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED at once when the op class is AML_CLASS_UNKNOWN (521-524), before any state is touched, and again for AML_TYPE_UNDEFINED (847-851). Otherwise it zeroes NumOperands, OperandIndex and ReturnDesc and ResultObj (531-534), calls AcpiDbSingleStep and returns its status directly if it fails (538-542). Then it switches on the class. AML_CLASS_ARGUMENT evaluates the name path only for AML_INT_NAMEPATH_OP (550-552). AML_CLASS_EXECUTE creates operands (a failure goes to Cleanup at 567 without calling AcpiDsClearOperands), resolves them unless the opcode has AML_NO_OPERAND_RESOLVE or lacks AML_HAS_ARGS, dispatches through AcpiGbl_OpTypeDispatch[OpType] on success, treats Store(LocalX,LocalX) of identical uninitialized local references as AE_OK (600-609), calls AcpiDsClearOperands (621) on every path that got past creation and pushes a non-NULL ResultObj on success (627-630). Other classes switch on the op type: control ops call AcpiDsExecEndControlOp; a method call whose parent is a Package or VarPackage op stores the node, adds a reference to the node's object and returns AE_OK immediately (652-662), skipping the cleanup at the end; a real method invocation creates and resolves operands, and if both succeed it returns AE_CTRL_TRANSFER immediately (707-713) leaving the operands on the stack for the called method and skipping the final NumOperands reset; if resolving fails it clears the operands (699). CreateField, CreateObject and the Named types call the AcpiDsLoad2EndOp / AcpiDsEval*Operands helpers, with the first failure ending that case; BOGUS does nothing; any other type gives AE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (867). Paths that reach 876 truncate a 32-bit table result, and on success evaluate a pending predicate (882-889). At Cleanup (893) a non-NULL ResultObj is shown and passed to AcpiDsDeleteResultIfNotUsed (906); a failure status is passed through AcpiDsMethodError (921); and NumOperands is set to 0 (926) before the final return. The ACPI_EXEC_APP block (732-749) is compiled only in that build. So: the final NumOperands = 0 and AcpiDsMethodError are not applied on the early returns at 524, 541, 662, 713 and 851.
note: reviewer RIGHT: dswexec.c:662 (package method reference) and 713 (AE_CTRL_TRANSFER) return before 926; also 567 skips AcpiDsClearOperands at 621; old prose said always clearing. Read whole function 500-928.

name: AcpiDsLoad1BeginOp
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsLoad1BeginOp(ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState, ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT **OutOp) at dswload.c:252-534 (slice cut the head). Precondition: WalkState has valid OpInfo, ParserState and ScopeInfo. OutOp is not read or written anywhere in the function. Postcondition: if WalkState->Op is already set and its opcode is not an AML_NAMED op, or it already has a Node, it returns AE_OK at once (272-286). Otherwise it reads the next name string from the parser state (289) and switches on the opcode. For AML_SCOPE_OP it looks the path up with AcpiNsLookup in execute mode with parent search (307); a lookup failure is returned (323-326) (the AE_NOT_FOUND retry at 309-321 exists only in the ASL compiler build); the found node's type must be Any, Scope, Device, Power, Processor or Thermal, or is reset to Any for Integer, String or Buffer (363-364), or a Method node is accepted only when it is the root node during module-level parsing (372-376), otherwise AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE is returned (389). For other opcodes: a WalkState->DeferredNode is used as the node (410-416), or, when MethodNode is set, the node is left NULL (423-427); otherwise it calls AcpiNsLookup in load-pass-1 mode with ACPI_NS_NO_UPSEARCH plus override-if-found or error-if-found flags chosen from NamespaceOverride and the deferred-op/scope conditions (430-461). On a failure other than AE_ALREADY_EXISTS the error is returned (493-496); on AE_ALREADY_EXISTS for a node marked ANOBJ_IS_EXTERNAL it clears that flag, sets the node type, pushes a scope if the type opens one (a push failure is returned) and changes the status to AE_OK (468-489); AE_ALREADY_EXISTS for a non-external node is returned as the status. After the switch, if Op is NULL it allocates one with AcpiPsAllocOp, returning AE_NO_MEMORY on failure (504-512); if Node is non-NULL it sets Op->Common.Node and Op->Named.Name from the node (521-529); it then appends the op to the parent scope's argument list (531) and returns Status (533), which is a success value on the paths that get there.
note: reviewer RIGHT-ish/MIXED on old prose (name not in slice); read whole function dswload.c:252-534, all returns listed (277,285,326,389,485,496,511,533).

name: AcpiDsLoad2BeginOp
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsLoad2BeginOp(ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState, ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT **OutOp) at dswload2.c:182-509 (slice cut the head). Precondition: WalkState has valid OpInfo, ParserState and ScopeInfo. OutOp is written only at line 500. Postcondition, in order: if WalkState->Op is set and a conditional is executing (ControlState state ACPI_CONTROL_CONDITIONAL_EXECUTING) it returns the status of AcpiDsExecBeginOp(WalkState, OutOp) (202-209). If Op is set but is not a named/namespace op (214-218), or is an AML_INT_NAMEPATH_OP whose Value.String is NULL (227-232), it returns AE_OK. Otherwise it picks the name string (Op's string, the op's Named.Name, or the next name string from the parser state, 227-246) and switches on the opcode. Field, BankField and IndexField ops use Node = NULL. A name-path op looks the string up with AcpiNsLookup in execute mode with parent search (272). A Scope op that is already the root node pushes it on the scope stack (a failure is returned, 285-288); otherwise it looks the name up (298) and returns the failure status (317), after logging with ACPI_ERROR_NAMESPACE (in the ASL compiler build, AE_NOT_FOUND is turned into AE_OK, which is then also returned at 317 before Node is stored); a Scope target of type Integer, String or Buffer gets its type reset to Any with a warning (348-354), a Method target is accepted only for the root node at module level, and any other type returns AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE (363-380). For other opcodes: if Op already has a Node, it pushes a scope when the type opens one (failure returned) and returns AE_OK without writing *OutOp (388-403); otherwise a DeferredNode is used, else AcpiNsLookup is called in load-pass-2 mode with flags built from PassNumber, module-level parsing and the AML_NAMED flag (423-466), and a failure is logged and returned (477-481). If Op is NULL it allocates one with AcpiPsAllocOp (AE_NO_MEMORY on failure, 488-491) and stores it in *OutOp (500). It then sets Op->Common.Node to the node and returns Status (507-508), a success value on that path.
note: reviewer RIGHT: *OutOp = Op only at dswload2.c:500 (inside Op-NULL block), and the Scope AE_NOT_FOUND (compiler build only) returns at 317 before Node is stored. Read whole function 182-509.

name: AcpiDsLoad2EndOp
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsLoad2EndOp(ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState) at dswload2.c:526-908, called at the end of an op during load pass 2 and also from AcpiDsExecEndOp. Precondition: WalkState->Op and OpInfo are valid. Postcondition: if the op's info lacks AML_NSOBJECT it returns AE_OK immediately and changes nothing (551-553). Otherwise it takes Node from the earlier lookup stored in Op->Common.Node (568) (it does no lookup itself except in the method-call case below), puts it in Operands[0] with NumOperands = 1 (574-575), and for an object type that opens a scope (other than AML_INT_METHODCALL_OP) pops the scope stack, jumping to Cleanup if the pop fails (579-588). It then switches on OpInfo->Type. CreateField calls AcpiDsCreateBufferField, failure goes to Cleanup (636-640). Named field: when running in a method (MethodNode set) AcpiDsInitFieldObjects is called (650), then the opcode picks AcpiDsCreateIndexField, CreateBankField or CreateField, whose status overwrites the earlier one (653-669); for any other opcode the status of AcpiDsInitFieldObjects (if it ran) is kept (671-674). Named simple: creates operands (failure to Cleanup, 680-683), then Processor, PowerResource, Mutex, Event or Alias creation via the AcpiEx helpers; an unknown opcode sets Status = AE_OK and jumps to Cleanup (717-718); on the other branches it releases the references on operands 1 and up and NULLs them (723-726). Named complex: Region and DataRegion call AcpiExCreateRegion only when MethodNode is set (a failure is returned at once, 766-770) and then call AcpiEvInitializeRegion on the node's attached object (774); Name op calls AcpiDsCreateNode (failure to Cleanup, 780-783); Method op, if the node has no attached object, creates operands and the method object, clears Operands[0] and NumOperands, and returns a failure at once (821-839). The internal class does nothing (855). The method-call class looks the call's name string up with AcpiNsLookup in load-pass-2 mode (866), requires a method type (AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE otherwise, 877-879), stores the node in Op->Common.Node (886), and logs a lookup failure with ACPI_ERROR_NAMESPACE (890). At Cleanup it sets Operands[0] = NULL and NumOperands = 0 (905-906) and returns Status; the early returns at 553 and 770 skip that reset (839 happens after its own reset).
note: reviewer WRONG: dswload2.c:866 does call AcpiNsLookup in the AML_CLASS_METHOD_CALL case (error logged at 890), so a lookup error exists for method calls; also Node for other ops comes from Op->Common.Node (568). Read whole function 526-908.

name: AcpiDsLoad2EndOp
prose: The slice (dswload2.c:774-908) is the tail of ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsLoad2EndOp(ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState), defined at dswload2.c:526-908; the packet name was not a function. This part covers the Region/DataRegion finish, the AML_NAME_OP and AML_METHOD_OP cases, the internal and method-call classes, and Cleanup. After the region case it calls AcpiEvInitializeRegion on the node's attached object (774). For AML_NAME_OP it calls AcpiDsCreateNode and jumps to Cleanup if that fails (780-783); in the ACPI_EXEC_APP build only (786-805) it then looks the node's pathname up in the init file, attaches the file's object if found (detaching any old one), frees the path and sets Status = AE_OK unconditionally. For AML_METHOD_OP, if the node has no attached object yet (821), it puts the node in Operands[0], calls AcpiDsCreateOperands on the op's argument list and, only if that succeeds, AcpiExCreateMethod (826-831); it then clears Operands[0] and NumOperands and returns a creation failure at once (834-839), skipping Cleanup. If the node already has an object, nothing is created. Other NAMED_COMPLEX opcodes do nothing (845-848). The AML_CLASS_INTERNAL case does nothing (855). The AML_CLASS_METHOD_CALL case calls AcpiNsLookup on the call's name string (866); on success a node whose type is not ACPI_TYPE_METHOD gives AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE (877-879), otherwise the node is saved in Op->Common.Node (886); on lookup failure the error is logged and Status stays the failure (890-891). Cleanup sets Operands[0] = NULL and NumOperands = 0 and returns Status (905-907).
note: slice cut the head, name was a placeholder; fixed under real name AcpiDsLoad2EndOp (526-908). reviewer RIGHT: AcpiDsCreateOperands failure returns at 839 (method case); init-file lookup failure still gives AE_OK at 804 (ACPI_EXEC_APP build only).

name: AcpiDsScopeStackPush
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiDsScopeStackPush(ACPI_NAMESPACE_NODE *Node, ACPI_OBJECT_TYPE Type, ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState) at dswscope.c:215-284 (slice cut the head). Precondition: WalkState is non-NULL (dereferenced without a check). Postcondition: if Node is NULL it logs an error and returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER without touching the walk state (227-232). If Type is not a valid object type it only logs a warning and carries on (237-240). It allocates a generic state with AcpiUtCreateGenericState and returns AE_NO_MEMORY if that fails, before changing the walk state (245-248). Otherwise it fills the new state as a scope state with the Node and Type (253-255), increments WalkState->ScopeDepth (257), pushes the new state onto WalkState->ScopeInfo (282, the previous scope stays below it) and returns AE_OK (283). The debug prints at 260-278 read the old scope and print only in debug builds.

name: AcpiEvAsynchExecuteGpeMethod
prose: static void ACPI_SYSTEM_XFACE AcpiEvAsynchExecuteGpeMethod(void *Context) at evgpe.c:645-731, run as a deferred OS task; Context is the ACPI_GPE_EVENT_INFO. Precondition: Context is a valid GPE event info. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It switches on ACPI_GPE_DISPATCH_TYPE(Flags) (660). For a NOTIFY dispatch it walks the notify list calling AcpiEvQueueNotifyRequest(DeviceNode, ACPI_NOTIFY_DEVICE_WAKE) for each entry, stopping at the first failure (674-680). For a METHOD dispatch it allocates a zeroed ACPI_EVALUATE_INFO (AE_NO_MEMORY on failure), evaluates the GPE method node with AcpiNsEvaluate ignoring any return value, frees the info and logs an exception on failure (688-710). For any other dispatch type it jumps to ErrorExit (716). After a NOTIFY or METHOD case, the status of that work is not used to choose the next step: it calls AcpiOsExecute(OSL_NOTIFY_HANDLER, AcpiEvAsynchEnableGpe, GpeEventInfo) (721) and returns if that succeeded (723-725), so the GPE is re-enabled later from the queued task; only if AcpiOsExecute fails, and for the default dispatch type, does it call AcpiEvAsynchEnableGpe directly (ErrorExit, 729), which takes AcpiGbl_GpeLock and calls AcpiEvFinishGpe (756-758).
note: reviewer RIGHT: default dispatch goes to ErrorExit at evgpe.c:716 and enables synchronously without trying AcpiOsExecute; but for NOTIFY/METHOD failures AcpiOsExecute is still tried (721). Read 645-760.

name: AcpiEvCreateGpeBlock
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiEvCreateGpeBlock(ACPI_NAMESPACE_NODE *GpeDevice, UINT64 Address, UINT8 SpaceId, UINT32 RegisterCount, UINT16 GpeBlockBaseNumber, UINT32 InterruptNumber, ACPI_GPE_BLOCK_INFO **ReturnGpeBlock) at evgpeblk.c:479-571 (slice cut the head). Precondition: GpeDevice is a namespace node; ReturnGpeBlock may be NULL. Postcondition: if RegisterCount is 0 it returns AE_OK at once and creates nothing, leaving *ReturnGpeBlock unwritten (496-498). Otherwise it allocates a zeroed ACPI_GPE_BLOCK_INFO, returning AE_NO_MEMORY on failure (503-506), and fills in the address, space id, node, GpeCount = RegisterCount * ACPI_GPE_REGISTER_WIDTH, RegisterCount and base number, with Initialized = FALSE (511-517). AcpiEvCreateGpeInfoBlocks failure frees the block and returns that status (523-527). AcpiEvInstallGpeBlock failure frees RegisterInfo, EventInfo and the block and returns that status (532-538). On success it sets AcpiGbl_AllGpesInitialized = FALSE (541), walks the namespace under GpeDevice for method objects with AcpiEvMatchGpeMethod, ignoring the walk's status (545-551), stores the block in *ReturnGpeBlock if that pointer is non-NULL (555-557), adds GpeCount to AcpiCurrentGpeCount (569) and returns AE_OK (570). The slice's second half (588-674) is the separate function AcpiEvInitializeGpeBlock, not described here.
note: packet had it dropped (name not in slice); function exists at evgpeblk.c:479-571, so fixed. No reviewer reason in packet. Read 479-570.

name: AcpiEvDetachRegion
prose: void AcpiEvDetachRegion(ACPI_OPERAND_OBJECT *RegionObj, BOOLEAN AcpiNsIsLocked) at evregion.c:506-657 (slice cut the head). Precondition: RegionObj is a region object. AcpiNsIsLocked says whether the caller holds the namespace mutex. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once, changing nothing, if the region has no secondary object (523-526) or no handler (532-537). Otherwise it scans the handler's region list for RegionObj (546-637). If found, it unlinks it with *LastObjPtr = ObjDesc->Region.Next and clears its Next field (558-559); if AcpiNsIsLocked it then releases the namespace mutex, returning at 566 if the release fails (the region is already unlinked, the handler is still set); it runs the _REG method with ACPI_REG_DISCONNECT (572), only logging a failure; it re-acquires the mutex if it had released it, returning at 584 if that fails (same partly detached state); and then, with the mutex held again, if AOPOBJ_SETUP_COMPLETE is set it calls the handler's Setup routine with ACPI_REGION_DEACTIVATE (592-596), sets *RegionContext = NULL if the pointer is non-NULL (602-605), logs but ignores a setup failure (609-614) and clears AOPOBJ_SETUP_COMPLETE (616). It finally sets RegionObj->Region.Handler = NULL and drops one reference on the handler object (628-629) and returns. If the end of the list is reached it prints a 'Cannot remove region' message (653, a debug print as written there) and returns (656); if the list loops back to its start it logs a circular-list error and returns (641-646), with no change to the region.
note: reviewer RIGHT: the Setup(DEACTIVATE) call at evregion.c:595 comes after AcpiUtAcquireMutex at 581, i.e. mutex is held again, not released. Read whole function 506-657.

name: AcpiUpdateAllGpes
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiUpdateAllGpes(void) at evxfgpe.c:187-225. Precondition: none on arguments; it uses the global GPE state. Postcondition: it acquires the ACPI_MTX_EVENTS mutex and returns that failure status if the acquire fails (197-200). If AcpiGbl_AllGpesInitialized is already TRUE it skips the work and returns the success status of the acquire (203-205, 224). Otherwise it calls AcpiEvWalkGpeList(AcpiEvInitializeGpeBlock, &IsPollingNeeded) (208), which enables the method-dispatch, non-wake GPEs of blocks not yet initialized, and sets AcpiGbl_AllGpesInitialized = TRUE only if the walk succeeded (210-212). It then releases the mutex, ignoring the release status (216). Only after that, if the walk flagged that polling is needed and AcpiGbl_AllGpesInitialized is TRUE, it calls AcpiEvGpeDetect on the GPE interrupt list head, ignoring the result (218-222). It returns the walk's status (or the acquire status on the already-initialized path) at 224.

name: AcpiExGenerateAccess
prose: static UINT32 AcpiExGenerateAccess(UINT32 FieldBitOffset, UINT32 FieldBitLength, UINT32 RegionLength) at exprep.c:203-331, which is compiled only when ACPI_UNDER_DEVELOPMENT is defined (exprep.c:172-332); in a normal build the function does not exist. Precondition: FieldBitOffset + FieldBitLength plus the byte rounding must not overflow 32 bits (no check is made). Postcondition: it computes the field's byte offset (round down to 8 bits, divided by 8), byte end offset (round up, divided by 8) and byte length (225-231), then tries access widths 1, 2, 4 and 8 in that order (247). For a width whose rounded-up end offset is within RegionLength (256), it computes the number of accesses as (end offset - start offset) in units of that width (259-267); if that is 1 or less, it returns that width immediately (278-284); otherwise it remembers the width as MinimumAccessWidth only when its access count is strictly smaller than the best so far (291-294), so on ties the narrower earlier width is kept. For a width whose end offset does not fit in the region, it returns 0 if that width is 1 (302-309) and otherwise returns MinimumAccessWidth (319), the remembered width. If the loop finishes without any return (width 8 fits but needs more than one access), it returns 8 (330), regardless of MinimumAccessWidth. Return values are therefore 0, a width from {1,2,4,8}, or 8.

name: AcpiNsLookup
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiNsLookup(ACPI_GENERIC_STATE *ScopeInfo, char *Pathname, ACPI_OBJECT_TYPE Type, ACPI_INTERPRETER_MODE InterpreterMode, UINT32 Flags, ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState, ACPI_NAMESPACE_NODE **ReturnNode) at nsaccess.c:436-927; this slice (518-781) is the middle of the function, covering prefix and path decoding and the first part of the segment loop. name: AcpiNsEvaluate
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiNsEvaluate(ACPI_EVALUATE_INFO *Info) at nseval.c:191-460 (slice cut the head). Precondition: Info is a valid evaluate info; Info->Node, or Info->PrefixNode with a pathname, identifies the object. Postcondition: a NULL Info returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER (200-202). If Info->Node is NULL it is resolved with AcpiNsGetNode (no upward search) and a failure is returned (205-219). A method-alias node is replaced by its target (227-230). It then clears Info->ReturnObject, copies the node flags, attached object and the predefined-name match into Info (235-245) and builds Info->FullPathname, returning AE_NO_MEMORY if that fails (249-252). It counts the NULL-terminated Parameters (at most ACPI_METHOD_NUM_ARGS, warning if more, 263-279) and runs the predefined-name compliance, argument-count and argument-type checks, ignoring their results (287-299). For a Method node it requires an attached object (otherwise AE_NULL_OBJECT, 336-341) and runs AcpiPsExecuteMethod inside AcpiExEnterInterpreter / AcpiExExitInterpreter (358-361). For Any, Device, Event, Mutex, Region, Thermal and Scope nodes it sets Status = AE_TYPE (326); both of these go to Cleanup (446). For any other node type it resolves the node's value through AcpiExResolveNodeToValue under the interpreter lock, sets Info->ReturnObject to the result, clears it and goes to Cleanup if resolution fails, and otherwise sets Status = AE_CTRL_RETURN_VALUE (388-404). The AE_TYPE, AE_NULL_OBJECT and resolve-failure paths skip that block via Cleanup, but Info->ReturnObject is NULL on each of them (set at 235 and 396). Cleanup frees Info->FullPathname, sets it to NULL and returns Status (457-459). On success of a value read, the caller gets the returned object (with a reference) in Info->ReturnObject.

name: AcpiNsCheckPackage
prose: ACPI_STATUS AcpiNsCheckPackage(ACPI_EVALUATE_INFO *Info, ACPI_OPERAND_OBJECT **ReturnObjectPtr) at nsprepkg.c:204-516 (the packet slice 254-505 is the middle of this function; the packet name AcpiNsCheckPackageTypes is not in the file). Precondition: *ReturnObjectPtr is a package object and Info->Predefined points at a predefined-name entry whose following entry (Package = Info->Predefined + 1, 222) describes the package layout. Postcondition: it first removes NULL elements with AcpiNsRemoveNullElements (233). An empty package returns AE_OK for ACPI_PTYPE1_VAR and AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE for every other type (244-254). It then switches on the layout type (263). CUSTOM calls AcpiNsCustomPackage. PTYPE1_FIXED returns AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE (via PackageTooSmall, 507-515) when there are fewer elements than Count1 + Count2, warns but continues when there are more, then returns AcpiNsCheckPackageElements. PTYPE1_VAR checks each element's type and returns the first failure. PTYPE2_REV_FIXED and PTYPE2_PKG_COUNT check that element 0 is an integer (first failure returned); the PKG_COUNT variant takes the count from that integer and returns AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE if it is not smaller than the element count; then AcpiNsCheckPackageList runs on the remaining elements. PTYPE2_UUID_PAIR requires an even count (otherwise AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE), then checks each pair: the first element's type, a 16-byte buffer length (AE_AML_OPERAND_VALUE if not 16, 474-478) and the second element's type, returning the first failure. Any other layout type warns and returns AE_AML_INTERNAL (501). Otherwise it returns the status from the helper (504).

name: AcpiPsGetNextArg

name: ar9300_fill_capability_info
prose: HAL_BOOL ar9300_fill_capability_info(struct ath_hal *ah) at ar9300_attach.c:2693-3088; the packet name ar9300_get_device_capabilities is not in the file and the slice (2910-3170) is the tail of this function plus ar9300_get_chip_power_limits and ar9300_config_pci_power_save.
